$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}>\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}>\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}>\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$

$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} < \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} < \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$

questions.solution:
- a. The thermal stability of hydrides of group 16 elements follows the order: \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} >  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} > \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} > \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}\) This is correct. As you go down the group, the central atom's size increases, and the E-H bond length increases. The bond becomes weaker and easier to break with heat, so thermal stability decreases.
- b. The acidic nature of hydrides of group 16 elements follows the order: \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} > \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} >  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} > \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}\) This is incorrect. The acidic nature increases down the group. As the E-H bond becomes weaker, it is easier to break, making it easier to donate a proton ( \(H^{+}\)). The correct order is \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} < \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} < \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} < \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}\).
- c. The reducing nature of \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}, \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}\), and \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}\) follows the order: \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} < \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} < \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}\) This is correct. The reducing nature increases as the E-H bond strength decreases down the group. It is easier for the hydride to donate hydrogen and get oxidized as the bond gets weaker.
